headline: Possible purchase of 14 to 16 Spring Street taken into executive session; 13 members voted in favor.
summary: The closed session covers the potential acquisition of 14 to 16 Spring Street and a related potential appropriation. Members will reopen the meeting to the public afterward, possibly to vote on that appropriation. Earlier, a zoning amendment for 181 through 185 Felton Street got a first reading, then was tabled. Approved finance items include $64,600 for a roof at the Lake Street fire station and $40,000 for professional services of Lillianne Winski.
decisions: Tabled until the end of the meeting the request to go into executive session on 14 to 16 Spring Street.
Approved the Salvation Army resolution for council members to ring bells on Friday, December 4.
Approved the Small Business Saturday resolution for Saturday, November 28th, 2026.
Tabled the resolution naming Joanne Raymond as the 2025 Kevin M. Ritzy Award recipient.
Tabled the resolution naming Douglas Wabry as the 2026 Kevin M. Ritzy Award recipient.
Approved the Suicide Prevention Awareness Month resolution, as recommended by the committee of the whole.
Approved a transfer of $64,600 for the roof replacement at the Lake Street fire station.
Approved a transfer of $42,536 for preliminary design of the firewall Street bridge repair.
Approved $6,760 to cover expanded work on the Chesterbrook Culvert at Beaver Street Lining Project.
Approved $40,000 for the professional services of Lillianne Winski.
Approved a first reading of the zoning amendment for 181 through 185 Felton Street.
Tabled the zoning amendment for 181 through 185 Felton Street after its first reading.
Approved a secondhand dealers license at 1275 Main Street.
Approved a secondhand dealers license at 550 Moody Street.
Approved extended-hours and license renewals for items three to nine together.
Approved going into executive session on 14 to 16 Spring Street, with 13 members in favor.
discussion: Salvation Army bell ringing: Members spoke in support of ringing bells for the Red Kettle Campaign on Friday, December 4, at Market Basket in Waltham, from 8.30 a.m. till 5 p.m. Speakers said the Salvation Army gives meals, backpacks, and Christmas toys to families in need.

Small Business Saturday: Speakers said local businesses give to charities and keep money in the community. One speaker described Watch City Pharmacy on Main Street, which got 15 minute parking spaces through the traffic commission for elderly customers.

Kevin M. Ritzy award: The 2025 and 2026 awards were tabled so they can be given at a time that works for the recipients. Councilors may sign on to the resolution, which the transcript says will be ready next Monday.
Veterans Day: A ceremony at the Circle of Remembrance starts at 11 a.m. on Wednesday, the 11th. The public is invited, and Veteran Services asked people to arrive around 10.30.
